definitions.note: here MP is the military police, not a member of parliament

parts.note: a socialist is often called a red
an international sportsman is awarded a cap, so a cap stands for an international

explanation.surface: A left-wing member of parliament who belongs to a global socialist body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MP' looks like a Member of Parliament, but it stands for Military Police. In Britain a player picked for the national side is 'capped', so CAP can mean an international.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcap is British slang for a military policeman, named after the red cap covers they wear.

definitions.meaning: slang for things to eat, as in a snack bar sign
the verb sense: something that troubles you is said to gnaw at you

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is casual slang for food, and the verb means to bother someone, as in 'what's bugging you'.

definitions.meaning: an old sense of the word is a whim or fanciful notion, so the plural names whims
a musical note worth one beat, called a quarter note in the US

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both odd fancies or whims and musical quarter notes, so the plural covers each reading.

definitions.meaning: slang for a jail, as in 'in the can'
Wormwood Scrubs is a well-known London jail, called here by the first half of its name

explanation.walkthrough: 'wormwood' looks like the bitter plant; it is Wormwood Scrubs, a jail in west London. The 'of' simply joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both 'can' (slang) and Wormwood Scrubs (an instance) refer to a jail.

definitions.meaning: a charger is an old word for a large flat serving dish
dated slang for vinyl gramophone discs

explanation.definitionFit: Large serving dishes are called chargers, and old slang called gramophone records by the same name as those dishes.

parts.note: reporters are the press, and to gather and talk together is to confer, so this is a meeting where the press confer

explanation.definitionFit: A media briefing where reporters assemble to question a speaker together.

parts.note: to fish with a rod and line is to angle

indicators.note: return tells us to read the next word backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round

explanation.surface: Someone asks where the fish swim back to and cheerfully confirms it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes!' looks like an exclamation answering the question, but 'return' turns it backwards; the island lies off north-west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglesey is an island off the north coast of Wales, an instance of the definition.

indicators.note: wounded suggests damage, so the letters of the two words before it are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A tear has been made in an injured soldier's jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wounded' rearranges the five letters of CUT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a close-fitting jacket worn as part of a military uniform.

clue.text: Plate make by Midas after the Revolution

definitions.text: Plate make by Midas after the Revolution

parts.words: Plate make by Midas after the Revolution
parts.note: King Midas turned what he touched to gold; read 'Revolution' as something turned over, and plate is thin metal coating

explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to mean a political revolution; read it as rolling. 'make' is probably a slip for 'made'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolled gold is a base metal with a thin layer of gold bonded on, a kind of plating.

clue.text: Without oxygen, operation could promote poison

indicators.note: could promote suggests the letters may be pushed into a new order
without tells us a letter is dropped from the word that follows it

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An operation done without oxygen might bring on poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes one O from OPERATION, leaving PERATION, and 'could promote' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a toxic alkaloid found in deadly nightshade, so it is a poison.

clue.text: Falcon is used to catch fish

definitions.meaning: a falcon-... is a trained falcon, especially a female peregrine
the word is also a soft maggot used as anglers' bait

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are rare: a falcon-gentle is a trained hawk, and a gentle is a maggot used by anglers as bait.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a trained falcon and a blowfly larva that anglers use for bait.

parts.note: an independent peer sits on neutral benches; 'bad-tempered' plays on 'cross' as angry

explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Lords, peers who belong to no party sit on the benches set across the chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-party member of the House of Lords, who sits on the benches across the chamber.

indicators.note: ruined suggests something wrecked, so the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alcohol has been the downfall of a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a French herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks.

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy' the piggies are toes, and what houses toes is footwear

explanation.walkthrough: 'little pigs' suggests a sty, but the piggies of the nursery rhyme are toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear such as a boot or a slipper is what houses the toes.

indicators.note: made here means formed anew, so the letters of the words after it are assembled differently

explanation.surface: A sponge is full of little holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Openings are gaps or holes in a surface.

clue.text: Home at some time or other will be under water

parts.note: to be home is to be in
something with no fixed date is undated

explanation.surface: A house will someday be flooded.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'under water'; 'will be' only links the wordplay to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooded land is covered by water, so something inundated is under water.

clue.text: Explorer who drops in for tea?

definitions.text: Explorer who drops in for tea?

parts.words: Explorer who drops in for tea?
parts.note: a caver drops down shafts; 'drops in for tea' suggests a social visit, or tea dropping into a teapot

explanation.definitionFit: A potholer is a caver who explores underground shafts, dropping down into them.

clue.text: How to deal with dandruff on cold shoulder?

definitions.meaning: flakes on the shoulders are removed by sweeping them away
a curt dismissal or snub

explanation.walkthrough: The 'on' joins the definitions and nods to dandruff on the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means sweep away flakes; as an idiom it means a snub.

annotationWithheld.why: Huge lady's headless! Not pretty (4): the blog gives only 'Huge lady minus head', and no word for a huge lady that loses its head to leave the answer can be found

clue.text: Crocodile's a hazard on the pavement

definitions.meaning: a broad-snouted crocodile of India
a street robber who attacks pedestrians

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an Indian marsh crocodile and a street robber.

clue.text: What the waiter did caused a stir

definitions.meaning: a waiter carries dishes to each table in turn
to revive someone who has fainted, making them stir again

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means carried dishes to people, and also revived someone from unconsciousness.

parts.note: a unit is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A group of soldiers from Europe assemble.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join together or combine.

definitions.meaning: to welcome or salute someone
Ibrox is the Glasgow Rangers stadium

explanation.walkthrough: Ibrox is the Glasgow Rangers football stadium, signalling a Scottish word for a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to salute, and in Scots it also means a goal scored.

clue.text: Woman miler running round the bend

indicators.note: round tells us the jumbled letters go around another piece
running suggests movement, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: a U-bend is a curve in a pipe, so a bend can give U

explanation.surface: An athlete on a track takes the curve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges MILER to MRIEL, and 'round' puts it around U.
explanation.definitionFit: Muriel is a woman's given name.

clue.text: A drink that goes to one's head

definitions.meaning: an alcoholic drink taken before bed
a soft hat worn in bed, literally on the head

explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to one's head' suggests intoxication, but means a cap worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bedtime drink and a soft cap worn in bed.

parts.note: an actor practises their part before a performance; it could also suggest crossing a boundary

explanation.definitionFit: To practise a play or speech before performing it is to run through it.

definitions.meaning: to permeate, as when something is ... with holes or errors
a conundrum or enigma

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to permeate thoroughly, and the noun is a conundrum.
